history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration complete the strategies for the nine remaining procurement categories.
history.administration_response: The Administration stated that the recommendation was under implementation. The Secretariat was currently evaluating how best to focus its resources across all the categories, with the aim of identifying the “core categories” where proactive end-to-end solutions for clients were sought, as opposed to “bespoke” categories where the Office of Supply Chain Management assisted clients with either guidance for local sourcing or assistance with implementing supply chain solutions tailored to a specific need. As such, a new schedule of strategy reviews for updates will be created in the coming months, which will also determine how and if the remaining four category strategies should be developed.
history.board_assessment: Work is still ongoing. The Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration complete the strategies for the nine remaining procurement categories.
history.administration_response: The Department of Operational Support refers to paragraph 312 of A/79/5 (Vol. I), in which the Board recommended the revision of the organization of the implementation of the 40 category strategies by classifying them as core or bespoke. The Administration accepted the recommendation and requests that this recommendation be considered overtaken by events.
history.board_assessment: In line with the recommendation issued in in paragraph 312 of A/79/5 (Vol. I), a prioritization of the procurement categories for which strategies must be implemented was applied, and this led to a review by the Administration. Core categories have been identified and strategies have been implemented for them, whereas bespoke categories will be treated through reactive approaches. Given that all core categories have approved strategies, the recommendation can be considered implemented.
